title: Introduction to Python
intro: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
bullets: Identify and use common Python datatypes, including strings, integers, floats, and Booleans.
Create, access, and change variables to store information in a program.
Use print() to display values in the console.
Use clear and descriptive names when creating variables.

title: Displaying Output with print()
paragraphs: The print() function displays information in the console.
Anything inside quotation marks is treated as text.

title: Variables
paragraphs: A variable is a named location that stores a value.
Variables allow programs to remember information and use it later.
Think of a variable as a labeled container: the variable name is the label, and the value is what is stored inside.

title: Variables vs. Literals
paragraphs: A literal is a value written directly in your code.
A variable stores a value under a name.
Both display 15, but the variable can be reused or changed later.

title: Datatypes
paragraphs: A datatype describes what kind of information a value contains.
The datatype determines how Python can use the value.
To the right are the most common primitive datatypes.
code:
name = "Alex"       # str
age = 15            # int
height = 1.72       # float
is_student = True   # bool

title: Strings (str)
paragraphs: A string stores text as a sequence of characters.
Strings must be surrounded by quotation marks.
Numbers surrounded by quotation marks are also treated as strings rather than numbers.

title: Numbers
paragraphs: Python commonly uses two datatypes for numbers.
An int stores a whole number, while a float stores a number with a decimal value.
Python determines which datatype to use based on the value being stored.

title: Integers (int)
paragraphs: An integer is a whole number without a decimal point.
Integers can be positive, negative, or zero.
They are useful for values that are counted using whole numbers.

title: Floats (float)
paragraphs: A float is a number that contains a decimal point.
Floats are useful for measurements and other values that may contain a fractional or decimal amount.

title: Booleans (bool)
paragraphs: A Boolean stores one of two possible values: True or False.
Booleans are commonly used to represent whether a condition is currently true or false.
In Python, True and False must begin with capital letters.

title: Initializing Variables
paragraphs: Initializing a variable means creating it and assigning its first value.
Python uses the equals sign (=) to assign a value to a variable.
The variable name goes on the left of =, and the value being stored goes on the right.

title: Naming Variables
paragraphs: Variable names should clearly describe the information they store.
Python variables should normally use snake_case, with lowercase words separated by underscores.
Use descriptive words instead of unclear abbreviations or single-letter names.

title: Accessing Variables
paragraphs: Accessing a variable means using the value currently stored inside it.
Use the variable's name whenever you want to access its value.

title: Changing Variables
paragraphs: A variable can be changed by assigning a new value to it.
The new value replaces the value that was previously stored.

title: Putting It Together
paragraphs: Variables allow programs to store information, access that information later, and change it as the program runs.
Each variable has a name, stores a value, and has a datatype based on the value being stored.
code:
player_name = "Alex"
score = 100
game_over = False

print(player_name)
print(score)

score = 150
print(score)

title: Wrap Up
bullets: Python stores values using datatypes such as int, float, str and bool.
Variables name values so you can access and change them.
Choose appropriate datatypes for the information your program stores.
Use print() to display values and program results.
